source: Built-in effect/SE example; DL variance and beta0 adjustment.
plain: This analysis combined 10 studies on the entered effect scale. The average effect from the random-effects model was 0.530. Extrapolation towards studies with no sampling error gave a limit estimate of 0.412 (95% confidence interval 0.238 to 0.586). The interval excludes no effect on this analysis scale. Differences between the estimates may reflect small-study effects; they do not establish publication bias, causation or clinical importance.
methods: Study effects and their standard errors were analysed on the entered scale, without transformation or continuity correction; ratio effects must already be entered on the log scale. Fixed-effect inverse-variance and random-effects inverse-variance estimates were calculated, with non-negative DerSimonian–Laird between-study variance (DerSimonian and Laird 1986). The tau-inflated standard error was the square root of the study variance plus tau-squared. The Rücker limit model used ordinary least squares radial regression of effect divided by the tau-inflated standard error on its reciprocal, including an intercept. The adjusted estimate was the radial slope plus tau times the radial intercept (the beta-zero adjustment). Its standard error was the square root of Var(slope) plus tau-squared times Var(intercept) plus twice tau times their covariance, using the closed-form inverse-variance design covariance without residual-scale inflation. All pooled 95% confidence intervals used the normal Wald formula, estimate plus or minus the normal critical value times its standard error, without Hartung–Knapp adjustment. The primary analysis computes no p-values, I-squared statistic or prediction interval. Cochran’s Q used fixed-effect weights; the small-study component was Q minus the raw-SE radial regression residual sum of squares. The residual component was that residual sum of squares; G-squared was one minus the squared correlation from the shrunken-study radial regression, and was unavailable when its total sum of squares was zero. Analyses were run in allmeta limit-ma <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: There were 10 studies. Fixed effect: 0.512 (SE 0.031; 95% CI 0.451 to 0.574). Random effects (DL): 0.530 (SE 0.043; 95% CI 0.446 to 0.615). Limit (Rücker): 0.412 (SE 0.089; 95% CI 0.238 to 0.586). Between-study variance tau-squared was 0.0072. No prediction interval was computed by the app.
flags: This report covers the primary fixed-effect, random-effects and limit analysis. Optional bias sensitivity comparisons are reported separately on the page.
references: DerSimonian R, Laird N. Meta-analysis in clinical trials. Control Clin Trials 1986;7:177-188.
